analyzed_vuln.description: CIL policy construction passes 32-bit symbol values into `__cil_insert_avrule`, which assigns `src`, `tgt`, and `obj` directly to the 16-bit fields of `avtab_key_t` without checking that they are representable. In this PoV, a type value reaches 65536 and is truncated to zero in `avtab_key.source_type`. The malformed key is inserted into `pdb->te_avtab`; later `is_avrule_redundant()` in `libsepol/src/optimize.c` computes `s_idx = source_type - 1`, underflowing to `UINT_MAX`, and reads far outside the allocated `type_map` at line 211. The crashing optimizer is therefore consuming invalid state created by the unchecked narrowing in `__cil_insert_avrule`.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Attacker-controlled CIL uses repeated/nested block inheritance to expand a compact input into a policy with more than 65535 type/type-attribute symbols, then causes an AV rule to reference a symbol whose policydb value is 65536 (or otherwise exceeds the 16-bit avtab-key range). `cil_build_policydb()` resolves that rule to a 32-bit value, `__cil_avrule_expand_helper()` forwards it to `__cil_insert_avrule()`, and the assignment to the 16-bit source/target field wraps (65536 becomes zero). The harness then calls `sepol_policydb_optimize()`, which indexes its type map using the wrapped key minus one and segfaults.

args: In selinux/libsepol/cil/src/cil_binary.c, analyze __cil_insert_avrule and its callers. What are the exact types/ranges of src, tgt, obj and avtab_key_t fields, how are errors propagated, and what existing project convention or constant should be used to reject values not representable in avtab keys? Also identify any analogous checked narrowing in this file or elsewhere in selinux/libsepol.

The reported crash occurs after CIL block inheritance creates over 65535 type symbols. __cil_avrule_expand_helper forwards 32-bit policydb values to __cil_insert_avrule, which stores them in 16-bit avtab_key_t source_type/target_type/target_class. A source value 65536 wraps to zero, and later optimize.c subtracts one and indexes out of bounds. I need a root-cause fix in C source that rejects invalid policy construction before insertion, preserving normal behavior and correctly propagating an error through cil_build_policydb.
